decision_reason: The repository contains a public Android application and an AGPL-3.0 grant for app-authored code, with a dated initial source commit and user manuals. Hold because the exact official CTT page is request-rejected in live retrieval and no accessible independent first-party source currently ties this repository/product to Suma’s public deployment.

government_provenance.note: The exact CTT product page is indexed with a description naming SuMaMatcher and Suma, but live retrieval returns Request Rejected. Suma’s live official site identifies Suma Gestión Tributaria as the Alicante provincial body, but it does not name this app or link this repository. The CTT organization listing places the repo under ctt-gob-es but does not by itself prove the product-specific relationship.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes an Android application tree, sample integration app, source, and documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE is GNU AGPL version 3. This supports the app-authored code grant only. The repository also bundles OpenALPR source with its own AGPL notice and native dependency binaries (including Tesseract/OpenCV-related components); those dependencies retain their own applicable terms and are not claimed covered by the root grant.

primary_evidence.note: The indexed official CTT record reports production from 2021-11-30 and describes a mobile plate-recognition app offered to public administrations, while the repository has user manuals through v1.2. Clearance path: accessible live/archived official product publication or an independent public-administration adoption record that explicitly names SuMaMatcher and ties it to Suma; do not rely on search-index text alone.

decision_reason: VALet is an identifiable certificate-validation module in the Spanish @firma suite and public source is available. Hold because an independent product identity/notability path and the full license scope of the nested license file have not been established separately from the parent suite.

government_provenance.note: The official CTT @firma description specifically lists VALet as the system for certificate validation against European Trusted Lists (TSLs), within the ministry-provided @firma platform.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes multiple Java/Maven modules, including valet-core, valet-rest, valet-web, and standalone statistics components.

eligible_license.note: The repository contains an EUPL-1.1 license text under resources/license and the core Maven POM references it for artifact metadata. The root does not provide a top-level license notice; repository-wide scope and component exceptions have not been verified for an independent VALet product record.

primary_evidence.note: The official page documents VALet’s function as a support element in @firma; the assigned repository has multiple deployable modules but no root README, standalone release page, or VALet-specific user/installation manual was found. Need direct evidence that VALet meets the baseline independently rather than duplicating the parent @firma product.

product_identity: VALet, @firma suite support component for validating certificates against European Trusted Lists (independent catalog identity unresolved)
agency: Secretaría General de Administración Digital (SGAD), Ministry for Digital Transformation and Public Function, as responsible body for the parent @firma platform
license: EUPL-1.1 text is present in resources/license/LICENSE.txt; repository-wide scope unresolved
family_note: VALet is listed as a component/support system within @firma; treat as one family with @firma unless independent distribution, installation guidance, or adoption is demonstrated.
status_note: The official CTT page describes @firma as a production, installable platform and identifies VALet as its TSL validation system. First public licensed functional source year was not established; repository creation date is not used as a substitute.
